title.narrative: HEARD - Förbättrad tillgång till SRHR för alla - 2018-2023
HEARD - Realisation of SRHR for all - 2018-2023

description.narrative:
HEARD, ett multidisciplinärt forsknings- och utbildningsinstitut vid University of KwaZulu-Natal, Sydafrika, har ansökt om finansiering från det regionala SRHR-teamet vid Ambassaden i Lusaka. Förslaget från HEARD omfattar ett fyraårigt program 2018-2021 till en kostnad motsvarande cirka 78 miljoner kronor.
Programmet syftar till att främja och stödja SRHR arbetet i södra och östra Afrika genom att generera ny kunskap och att stödja användningen av kunskap i beslutsfattande inom hälsa och SRHR-området. HEARD syftar till att (i) minska avståndet mellan forskning och beslutsfattare, (ii) genomföra riktad, tillämpad, forskning för att göra politiska och finansiella investeringar inom SRHR mer effektiva. (iii) skapa en regional plattform för evidensbaserat beslutsfattande inom SRHR och hälsa.
HEARD kommer inom ramen för interventionen att bedriva tillämpad forskning, genomföra forskningsutbildningar och utbildningar för beslutsfattare och slutligen bedriva påverkansarbete gentemot beslutsfattare.
Ambassaden har samarbetat med HEARD sedan drygt tio år tillbaka och under den senaste insatsperioden (2011-2017) har Ambassaden gett HEARD kärnstöd. Det är ambassadens bedömning att HEARD under kommande projektperiod måste minska sitt beroende av kärnfinansiering från Sverige och skapa en långsiktigt hållbar grund för finansiering.

Then intervention comprises support to HEARD at the University of KwaZulu-Natal, SA, for advancing SRHR priorities across the Eastern and Southern Africa (ESA) region. The overarching goal of the intervention is to ensure that the uptake of robust, comprehensive evidence drives improvement in SRHR across ESA.
Support the generation and use of robust evidence by national and regional stakeholders working to improve Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) across East and Southern Africa.

1. Workstream 1: Applied research Over the five and a half year Sida contract period, HEARD conducted research on the SRHR of key and vulnerable populations in East and Southern Africa, contributing to scientific knowledge in the areas of adolescent contraceptive access and unsafe abortion LGBTI social exclusion and implications for LGBTI SRHR, and gender based violence and implications for women and girls SRHR. HEARD also produced analysis of the investment landscape for SRHR within UHC, including the likely implications of the COVID19 pandemic for SRHR financing. HEARD further considered how the COVID19 pandemic response was having adverse consequences for SRHR outcomes. Over half the publications were HIV focused, in large part due to publications resulting from HEARDs work and research on HIV and AIDS in the years preceding and overlapping with the 2018-2023 funding period. In total, HEARD published two authored books (on SRHR in Sub-Saharan Africa and on HIV and young people in Sub-Saharan Africa), four book chapters (all on HIV/AIDS in Sub-Saharan Africa), and 167 articles (with 52% in journals ranked as those with highest impact, so-called Q1 journals). HEARD also produced 36 policy briefs and more than 40 research reports that were made publicly available. Other achievements under this workstream include 60 civil society organisations being supported by HEARD with data, analysis and tools resulting from HEARDs research, and HEARD presenting 45 research papers across 34 scientific conferences and seminars, hosted in 12 different countries.
Workstream 2: Capacity strengthening HEARDs capacity strengthening took the form of Ministerial retreats, virtual ministerial meetings, and workshops. Ministerial retreats: HEARD was able to host three of the four ministerial retreats planned for the contract period COVID19 restrictions meant one retreat could not take place. One example of this is that HEARD, in partnership with UNAIDS and the Champions former African Heads of State and other influential African leaders hosted a high level roundtable dialogue in 2018 in South Africa to examine the current domestic funding environments for the AIDS response and to seek innovative sources of domestic revenue to bridge the gap in health financing. To inform this dialogue, HEARD developed a policy brief making a case for advancing political leadership for domestic investment in sustaining the AIDS response in Africa as well as produced the outcomes document following the meeting.
Workshops/courses: In addition, HEARD either arranged or co-arranged 24 workshops/courses between 2018-2021 on topics such as translating evidence based research into policy briefs for decision makers, SRHR in UHC and access to safe abortion care.
Workstream 3: Regional networking, advocacy and technical support HEARDs overarching goal for the 2018-2023 strategy period was to support the generation and use of robust evidence by national and regional stakeholders working to improve SRHR across East and Southern Africa. HEARD has recorded 94 instances over the contract period where HEARD data and analysis has contributed to decision, policy, or programme making processes or outcomes. 54 of HEARDs 94 engagements involved technical assistance, which was by far HEARDs most prolific form of engagement. HEARDs advisory assistance and advocacy approaches, which frequently overlapped, were used in 24 engagements each. HEARD convened governments and regional organisations on 12 occasions to discuss pressing issues.
Workstream 4: PhD programme The HEARD Sida PhD scholarship programme intended to support 60 students to complete their doctorates in the area of health policy and practice. In total, 39 candidates were enrolled between 2018 and 2022 against the initial target of 60 enrollments over the period. 11 candidates submitted their research theses for examination (completed) between 2018 and 2022. Six candidates took five years to complete, and one candidate took six years to complete due to maternity leave.
HEARD exceeded its targets for providing (non-doctoral) research and training support. It delivered 26 health management, planning and policy workshops for health and development actors and researchers, against a target of 16, between 2018-2021.. In total, 357 health and finance officials and health and development actors were trained in health management, against a target of 160, and 285 academics and researchers were trained in advanced research skills and/or health policy.
